A molecular-level hypothesis has been proposed: for every $2e^-$ transferred through the electron-transfer chain, Complex III transports $2HSuc^-$ across the membrane. The opposing concentration gradients that must be overcome in the two transport events are approximately $1:7$ and $1:8$, respectively. Energy losses from other ion-transport processes at Complexes I and IV may be neglected. The inner-side condition is $pH=8$, the outer-side condition is $pH=5$, succinic acid has $pK_{a1,2}=4.2,5.6$, and the temperature is $310\,\mathrm{K}$.
For this redox reaction, $\Delta_rG_m^{\ominus *}\approx-2.20\times10^2\ \mathrm{kJ\,mol^{-1}}$; take the magnitude of the available energy as $220\ \mathrm{kJ\,mol^{-1}}$.
ATP synthase can transport only $HSuc^-$ ions on the outer side of the membrane; neither $H_2Suc$ nor $Suc^{2-}$ outside the membrane can pass through ATP synthase. Thus, of the energy stored in $H_2Suc$, $HSuc^-$, and $Suc^{2-}$ during the redox stage, only the fraction associated with external $HSuc^-$ can be utilized. On this basis, calculate $\eta_{redox}$.
